content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin, Python scripting

[EMAIL] | [PHONE]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with professional experience building and operating Java and Kotlin services, with a focus on REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing and reliable production systems. Experienced in on-call support, service extraction and event-processing reliability. Uses Python for scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and is building a Go CLI as a side project. Interested in moving to a backend role working mainly in Python.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java, Kotlin; Python (scripts and small Jenkins helpers); Go (learning; side project)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, REST API design, OpenAPI 3, microservices
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis, AWS S3, AWS SQS
Cloud and containers: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker; AWS services as a user
Testing: Testcontainers, Spring Cloud Contract, contract testing
Other: On-call incident response; Terraform (can read, has not written modules)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | 2022–Present
- Build and support Java and Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using Kafka, PostgreSQL and Kubernetes.
- Designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for broker quote requests; added per-partner rate limiting and contract tests using Spring Cloud Contract. The API serves 12 broker partners and around 400,000 quote requests per month.
- Resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox pattern and idempotency keys for consumers. Duplicate claims fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
- Built the company's first Kotlin service, an internal Spring Boot document service that renders policy PDFs from templates; wrote Kotlin coding guidelines for the team.
- Participate in an on-call rota one week per month. Handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and produced a write-up that was praised.
- Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).

Software Developer | Viajar Online | 2019–2021
- Worked on the booking and payments parts of a large Java application.
- Increased payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring.
- Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot service using RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.

PROJECTS
OpenAPI Specification Diff CLI | Personal side project
- Building a Go command-line tool to compare OpenAPI specifications; approximately 600 lines of code and available on GitHub. Side project, not production software.

CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer | 2020

LANGUAGES
English: Worked in an English-speaking environment at Tejo Insurance Tech.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, honest, achievement-focused CV with clear progression from Java development into backend engineering. The quantified API and Kafka results are particularly persuasive, and the document communicates relevant production experience, on-call responsibility, testing, messaging, and reliability work. The main weaknesses are that the contact details are still placeholders, some important technologies appear only in the skills section rather than in experience bullets, and the CV does not clearly distinguish demonstrated production experience from limited exposure in areas such as Python, AWS deployment, and Terraform.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column structure, standard section headings, plain-text bullets, and conventional chronology are ATS-friendly. The CV includes strong matching terms such as Python, Java, Kotlin, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, OpenAPI, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, EKS, AWS, automated testing, Testcontainers, Spring Boot, and Terraform. ATS alignment would improve if the experience section explicitly included terms already supported by the candidate's material, such as AWS S3/SQS, Redis, Oracle, Jenkins, CI/CD-related helpers, and Java 17. Do not add FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or schema migrations because the candidate information does not support those claims. The current placeholder email and phone number also make the CV incomplete for parsing and application submission.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a credible match for the comparable-language route in the advertisement: the candidate has more than three years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and clearly states an interest in moving mainly into Python. PostgreSQL, REST API design, Docker, Kafka, Kubernetes/EKS, automated testing, production incidents, and technical documentation align well with the role. The quantified API scale and duplicate-claim reduction are relevant evidence for reliable event-driven services. The main job-alignment gaps are professional Python service development, demonstrated query tuning and live schema migrations, explicit CI/CD ownership, observability tooling, logistics or EDI knowledge, and Dutch/French language skills. These are candidate-background gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording. The on-call cadence is one week per month rather than the advertised one week in six, but it still demonstrates relevant production-support experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the contact-information line at the top of the CV, replace "[EMAIL]" and "[PHONE]" with the candidate's actual professional email address and phone number before submitting.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Professional Summary, make the comparable-language qualification more explicit and ATS-readable without overstating Python experience. For example, change the final sentence to: "Interested in moving into a backend role working mainly in Python, bringing more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and hands-on Python scripting experience." Keep the existing wording that distinguishes scripts from production Python services.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, revise the first bullet to include the supported cloud and database context: "Build and support Java and Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis and Kubernetes on AWS EKS." This makes the existing AWS/Kubernetes experience more visible without claiming ownership of AWS infrastructure.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Viajar Online experience section, revise the notifications-service bullet to include the supported deployment and database technologies: "Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot service using RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf, with Docker and Oracle." This places Docker and Oracle in experience context rather than leaving them dependent on keyword scanning in other sections.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Technical Skills section, change "Cloud and containers: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker; AWS services as a user" to "Cloud and containers: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker; AWS S3 and SQS (user-level experience)" because S3 and SQS are specifically supported by the candidate material. Retain the qualification that the AWS platform team handled Terraform.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Technical Skills section, add a separate entry such as "CI/CD and tooling: Jenkins helpers/scripts" only if the intention is to expose the existing small Jenkins-helper experience. Do not label this as CI/CD pipeline ownership or GitHub Actions experience, since the candidate material does not establish either claim.

MINOR/TARGETED: In the Languages section, replace "English: Worked in an English-speaking environment at Tejo Insurance Tech" with the more informative supported wording: "English: Worked in an English-speaking environment at Tejo Insurance Tech; used English as the working language." This better supports the advertisement's English requirement without claiming a formal language certification.
critique.critical_issues: The CV is not application-ready because the email address and phone number are placeholders: "[EMAIL] | [PHONE]". Replace them with the candidate's real contact details. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected; the claims about Python scripting, Go, AWS user-level exposure, Terraform limitations, Kubernetes/EKS, Kafka, and the quantified outcomes are consistent with the original candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and appropriately honest about the candidate's Python and Go experience. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including 400,000 quote requests per month, a reduction in duplicate claims from approximately 40 per week to zero, and increased test coverage from 35% to 70%. The experience section demonstrates backend ownership, production support, event-processing reliability, API design, automated testing, and service extraction. The main content limitation is that the CV does not demonstrate PostgreSQL query tuning or schema migrations, and it provides only limited evidence of CI/CD beyond Jenkins helper scripts. The Python positioning is transparent and credible, but the candidate is not presented as someone who has already shipped Python services.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text bullets, recognizable technology names, and measurable achievements. Relevant keywords such as Python, Java, Kotlin, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, OpenAPI, Kafka, Docker, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, CI/CD, Jenkins, and Terraform are present. AI screening probability is reasonably strong for a comparable-language backend profile, but likely lower for screening models prioritizing professional Python service development, FastAPI, GitHub Actions, database migrations, or query tuning. The skills section is accurate but slightly repetitive: AWS S3 and SQS appear in both the data/messaging and cloud sections, while AWS itself is not used as the main cloud label in the Cloud section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate aligns strongly with the comparable-language experience requirement through more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend work and explicitly states an interest in working mainly in Python. The CV also aligns well with REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, automated testing, Kafka, Kubernetes, limited Terraform exposure, production incidents, and English-language work. The candidate's experience with at-least-once Kafka delivery, idempotency, transactional outbox design, on-call support, and incident write-ups fits the role's reliability and event-ingestion focus. Gaps shown by the candidate's material are professional Python service development, PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, observability tooling, logistics or supply-chain experience, EDI formats, and Dutch or French. These are job-alignment gaps rather than document defects. The CV does not claim unsupported experience with FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, EDI, or logistics.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS AND CLARITY ENHANCEMENT: In the Technical Skills section, consolidate the duplicated AWS entries. Change the Cloud and containers line to "Cloud and containers: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Kubernetes, Docker" and change the Data and messaging line to "Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis". This keeps the information accurate while making AWS easier for ATS screening to identify as the cloud platform.

MINOR POSITIONING ENHANCEMENT: In the Professional Summary, replace "Interested in moving into a backend role working mainly in Python, bringing more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and hands-on Python scripting experience" with "Seeking a backend role working mainly in Python, bringing more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and hands-on Python scripting experience." This is more direct while preserving the important truthful distinction that the Python experience is scripting rather than shipped Python services.

MINOR KEYWORD CLARIFICATION: In the Technical Skills section, change "CI/CD and tooling: Jenkins helpers/scripts" to "CI/CD and tooling: Jenkins helper scripts; CI/CD support" only if the existing Jenkins helper work genuinely supported a CI/CD process. If not, retain the current wording; do not imply ownership of Jenkins pipelines that the candidate did not have.

- About the employer: "large Java application"

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible, well-structured CV with clear progression, relevant backend experience, measurable outcomes, and unusually good honesty about Python, Go, AWS, and Terraform proficiency. The strongest evidence includes the 400,000 monthly API requests, reduction of duplicate claims to zero, test-coverage increase from 35% to 70%, on-call experience, and service extraction work. The summary is well targeted to a Python-transition role without falsely claiming production Python service experience. Minor content limitations are that CI/CD contribution, REST API consumption, and technical trade-off communication are not stated as explicitly as they could be. The CV also does not include a location, LinkedIn profile, or GitHub URL, although these are not necessarily defects based on the provided information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text structure, conventional job-title formatting, and relevant searchable terms including Java, Kotlin, Python, Spring Boot, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, Testcontainers, OpenAPI, and Jenkins. Keyword coverage is strong for the comparable-language route and event-driven backend work. AI screening probability is good for a backend engineer role accepting Java/Kotlin experience, but more moderate for a strictly Python-focused screen because the CV explicitly states that Python has only been used for scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and it does not mention FastAPI. The PostgreSQL requirement's query-tuning and schema-migration terms are also absent. Do not add those terms unless supported by additional verified experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Overall alignment is strong for the job's comparable-language pathway. The document clearly shows more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience, production REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, Kafka, Kubernetes/EKS, automated testing, on-call incident response, and English-language work. It also demonstrates reliability-oriented work that fits the company's values, including idempotency, transactional outbox design, incident handling, and service ownership. The candidate's material shows no professional Python service experience, no FastAPI experience, no confirmed PostgreSQL query tuning or schema migration experience, no observability tooling experience, no logistics/transport/supply-chain or EDI experience, and no Dutch or French. Terraform is only a read-level skill and not hands-on module development. These are candidate-background gaps rather than CV defects. The CV could make the supported CI/CD and technical communication evidence more explicit without overstating it.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the comparable-language qualification more directly match the advert while preserving the truthful Python limitation. Replace the final two sentences with: "Seeking a backend role working mainly in Python, bringing more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and hands-on Python scripting experience." If retaining the existing wording, ensure "working mainly in Python" remains visible because it directly addresses the advert's comparable-language pathway.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Tooling: Jenkins helpers/scripts" to "CI/CD and tooling: Jenkins helpers/scripts" only if these scripts were used in the team's delivery or build workflow, as indicated by the candidate's notes. This improves ATS matching for CI/CD without claiming ownership of a CI/CD platform or pipeline that is not documented.

3. In the Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, revise the on-call bullet to make the incident-documentation evidence more searchable and precise: "Participate in an on-call rota one week per month; handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and produced a written incident report that was praised." Do not call it a blameless post-mortem unless that is factually accurate.

4. In the Professional Summary or the relevant Tejo Insurance Tech bullet, make the documented API work explicitly searchable as "REST API" rather than relying only on "REST APIs" in the summary. For example, retain or revise the bullet to: "Designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for broker quote requests; added per-partner rate limiting and contract tests using Spring Cloud Contract." This is already supported and improves exact keyword matching.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In the Languages section, change "English: Worked in an English-speaking environment at Tejo Insurance Tech; used English as the working language" to "English: Professional working proficiency; used English as the working language at Tejo Insurance Tech." This more directly matches the advert's written-and-spoken-English wording without claiming a formal language level.

6. In the Professional Experience section under Viajar Online, change "Increased payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring" to "Increased automated test coverage in the payments module from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring." This makes the automated-testing evidence more ATS-readable.

7. In the Projects section, format the GitHub reference as an actual visible URL or profile link if one is available. The current phrase "available on GitHub" is credible but gives a recruiter no direct way to inspect the project. Do not add a fabricated URL.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured and professional CV. It presents a clear backend profile, uses measurable outcomes effectively, and gives credible technical detail without overstating Python or Go experience. The strongest evidence includes the 400,000 monthly API requests, the reduction of duplicate claims from approximately 40 per week to zero, the increase in test coverage from 35% to 70%, and the service-extraction work. The CV also communicates operational ownership through on-call support, incident handling, and reliability improvements. Completeness is good for the candidate's documented experience, although the profile is substantially stronger in Java/Kotlin than in production Python.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, simple text structure, clear job titles, standard date ranges, and relevant searchable terms such as Python, Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot, REST API, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, Testcontainers, RabbitMQ, and Terraform. Its AI-screening probability is good for a comparable-language backend role and moderate for a Python-first role because the document correctly shows only scripting-level Python experience and no production Python service development. The CV does not claim unsupported technologies such as FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, or OpenTelemetry, which preserves credibility. A few truthful wording refinements could make matching more precise, particularly by using the exact phrases “designing REST APIs,” “automated testing,” and the relevant Java versions.

The candidate clearly demonstrates more than five years of backend experience in Java/Kotlin, REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS deployment through EKS, Kafka, Kubernetes, automated testing, on-call incident response, and English-language work. The reliability and ownership evidence also fits the company's culture: dependable services, production support, incident write-ups, documentation, and technical community contribution. The candidate's material does not demonstrate query tuning, schema migrations, production Python services, explicit CI/CD ownership, observability tooling, logistics or supply-chain experience, EDI formats, or Dutch/French language skills. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The document appropriately avoids presenting them as existing experience.
